# CodeArts build

The user's goal is in the arguments of this skill (or the message that invoked it). If there is
no goal, ask for one in a single question, then start.

## Tools

Use the `codearts` MCP server tools: `mcp__codearts__ca_doctor`, `ca_init`, `ca_workspace`,
`ca_lane_start`, `ca_status`, `ca_wait`, `ca_summary`, `ca_tail`, `ca_steer`, `ca_stop`, `ca_plan`,
`ca_plan_update`, `ca_note` (all prefixed `mcp__codearts__`). Below they are named without the
prefix.

Register the plan you are working to with `ca_plan` as soon as you start, and keep it current:
`ca_plan_update` for a changed goal, next tasks or lanes, and `ca_note` (now true, with phase
planning, building, waiting, verifying, asking or done) for a meaningful transition. The plan is how
the human follows the work in both dashboard views, so publish real scope changes and transitions,
not a heartbeat, and never paste private reasoning or chat.

- Before you end your turn to ask the human anything (a question, a choice, an approval), post
  `ca_note {now: true, phase: 'asking', text: '<the question in one line>'}`; when work resumes,
  post the next phase. The dashboard shows it as Needs you.

Preflight: run `ca_doctor` before the first lane. A `repo writable` fail row stops everything (on
Windows allow git, Git Bash and node in Defender's Controlled Folder Access, or move the repo out of
Documents), otherwise every commit fails.

Run: in `ca_wait`, wait with `any: true` when lanes run in parallel, so an early failure is seen at
once (the finished lanes come back, the rest as still running).

Parallel lanes: give each its own clone with `ca_workspace {repo, task, from}` (CLI
`ca workspace <repo> <task> [--from <branch>]`), which makes `../<repo>-wt-<task>` on branch
`lane/<task>`, then start the lane in that folder. Never use `git worktree add` for a lane: a
worktree keeps its git dir in the main repo, outside the lane folder, so the CodeArts sandbox
refuses every commit ("Permission denied"). Merge a clone back with `ca_workspace --land {repo, task}`.

If those tools are missing, the server is not connected: tell the user to run
`ca onboard --yes --harness claude` once and restart Claude Code (or `/mcp` to reconnect). Until
then the same steps work from the shell with the `ca` CLI (`ca doctor`, `ca init`,
`ca lane --detach`, `ca wait`, `ca summary`); see `ca --help`.

A repo that is not a git repo yet is fine: `ca onboard --yes --harness claude` (or `git init`
plus an empty first commit) fixes it, and `ca lane` trusts the folder by itself.

Never print, log or commit credentials (`CODEARTS_CLI_AK`, `CODEARTS_CLI_SK`, `MAAS_API_KEY`).
